answer: Physical resource mirror. Each identity must continuously mirror a distinct allocated slice of real compute and bandwidth on hardware whose serial numbers a single operator cannot duplicate across machines. A wharf-side sensor logs the physical machine's power draw against its claimed work, so one operator cannot fake the mirror across many identities without buying many machines. Each extra identity therefore costs a full physical host plus its power ceiling, and a scraped relic of another host's serial fails the draw check within one cycle.
